messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE:

Admitted from the emergency room due to severe dyspnea, a 69-year-old Japanese man was diagnosed with aspiration pneumonia and placed on mechanical ventilation. He underwent tracheostomy due to prolonged mechanical ventilation and had restrictive pulmonary dysfunction. He was weaned successfully from mechanical ventilation with support by HFT (flow at 40 L/minute with FIO2 of 0.25) and a ventilator (10 cmH2O pressure support with 5 cmH2O PEEP) at night. The patient was discharged from the ICU to the general ward on ICU day 51. His physiotherapy rehabilitation continued for 1 month.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES: [diagnosis section withheld]
TREATMENT:

Mechanical ventilation, tracheostomy, and respiratory support by HFT and a ventilator.

FOLLOW-UP AND RECOMMENDATIONS:

The patient was discharged to home on day 86 of hospitalization and returned for a follow-up visit. No further recommendations were provided.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The principal diagnosis is aspiration pneumonia, which is coded to J69 (pneumonitis due to solids and liquids).

The case describes a 69-year-old man admitted with severe dyspnea and diagnosed with aspiration pneumonia. He then needed mechanical ventilation, a tracheostomy and prolonged ICU care. The restrictive pulmonary dysfunction and ventilator weaning are consequences or complications of that illness, so they do not replace it as the principal diagnosis. The diagnosis section was withheld, but the hospital course states the admitting diagnosis clearly.

J69
